<ns0:oval_definitions xmlns:ns0="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-definitions-5" xmlns:ns1="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-common-5" xmlns:ns2="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-definitions-5#unix"><ns0:generator>
        <ns1:product_name>Security Content Tool 1.9.0</ns1:product_name>
        <ns1:schema_version>5.11</ns1:schema_version>

      <ns0:definitions><ns0:definition id="oval:mil.disa.stig.defs:def:230534" version="1" class="compliance">
          <ns0:metadata>
            <ns0:title>The root account must be the only account having unrestricted access to the operating system system.</ns0:title>
            <ns0:description />
          </ns0:metadata>
          <ns0:criteria>
            <ns0:criterion test_ref="oval:mil.disa.stig.unix:tst:23053400" comment="Only the root account has a UID of zero." />
          </ns0:criteria>
        </ns0:definition>
        <ns0:definition id="oval:mil.disa.stig.rhel9os:def:258059" version="3" class="compliance">
          <ns0:metadata>
            <ns0:title>RHEL-09-411100 - The root account must be the only account having unrestricted access to RHEL 9 system.</ns0:title>
            <ns0:affected family="unix">
              <ns0:platform>Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9</ns0:platform>
            </ns0:affected>
            <ns0:description>An account has root authority if it has a user identifier (UID) of "0". Multiple accounts with a UID of "0" afford more opportunity for potential intruders to guess a password for a privileged account. Proper configuration of sudo is recommended to afford multiple system administrators access to root privileges in an accountable manner.</ns0:description>
          </ns0:metadata>
          <ns0:criteria>
            <ns0:extend_definition definition_ref="oval:mil.disa.stig.defs:def:230534" />
          </ns0:criteria>
        </ns0:definition>
        </ns0:definitions><ns0:tests><ns2:password_test id="oval:mil.disa.stig.unix:tst:23053400" version="1" check="all" comment="Only the root account has a UID of zero.">
          <ns2:object object_ref="oval:mil.disa.stig.unix:obj:23053400" />
          <ns2:state state_ref="oval:mil.disa.stig.unix:ste:23053400" />
        </ns2:password_test>
        </ns0:tests><ns0:objects><ns2:password_object id="oval:mil.disa.stig.unix:obj:23053400" version="1">
          <ns2:username operation="not equal">root</ns2:username>
        </ns2:password_object>
        </ns0:objects><ns0:states><ns2:password_state id="oval:mil.disa.stig.unix:ste:23053400" version="1">
          <ns2:user_id datatype="int" operation="not equal">0</ns2:user_id>
        </ns2:password_state>
        </ns0:states></ns0:oval_definitions>
